overview.title: A ceremonial façade on the city's main square
overview.p1: The Royal Palace of Tetouan (Dar al-Makhzen) stands at the edge of Place Hassan II, marking the transition between the Spanish Ensanche and the historic medina. Its white walls, green-tiled roofs and ornate gates embody the Hispano-Moorish style that defines much of northern Morocco's official architecture.
overview.p2: The interior remains an active royal residence and is closed to the public. Visitors enjoy the grand exterior, the ceremonial gates and the lively atmosphere of the square itself.
overview.p3: Combine a visit with a walk into the medina through the nearby gates or continue to the Modern Art Museum and archaeological sites nearby.

q1.question: Can visitors enter the Royal Palace?
q1.answer: No, the interior is an active royal residence and is closed to the public. Visitors can admire and photograph the grand exterior and gates from Place Hassan II.

q2.question: Is there an admission fee?
q2.answer: No fee is required since it is viewed freely from the public square (Place Hassan II).

q3.question: What is the best time to visit?
q3.answer: Late afternoon provides wonderful golden light on the palace walls and a lively atmosphere on Place Hassan II.

q4.question: How long should I spend here?
q4.answer: 20 to 40 minutes is enough to enjoy the façade, take photos and absorb the square.

q5.question: Is it close to the medina?
q5.answer: Yes. The main medina gates open directly from the area around Place Hassan II.
